key_insight: MonoIR-RS fills a major gap in vision-language research by bringing infrared remote-sensing data into the CLIP/VLM ecosystem. It shows that IR imagery can support meaningful language grounding and evaluation when the data and adaptation strategy are designed for infrared-specific cues.
problem_solved: Most remote-sensing vision-language datasets and models are built around visible-band imagery, while infrared remote sensing remains underexplored. This paper addresses the lack of large-scale IR-aware data and benchmarks for training and evaluating vision-language models on infrared scenes.
method: Builds MonoIR-RS, a large-scale infrared remote-sensing vision-language dataset and benchmark.
Designs IR-aware data construction to capture intensity structure, object-background contrast, and illumination-invariant cues.
Adapts CLIP-style contrastive learning and VLM-based methods to better align infrared images with text.
impact: For practitioners, this provides a new benchmark for testing whether vision-language models generalize beyond RGB and into infrared sensing. It can improve remote-sensing applications such as scene understanding, cross-modal retrieval, and downstream decision support in conditions where visible imagery is limited.

paper_title: MonoIR-RS: Infrared Remote Sensing Vision-Language Learning with CLIP and VLM Adaptation
paper_authors: Jiaju Han, Ma Yaqi, Yahui Chai, Xuemeng Sun, Xin Li
